claims: Constant horizontal speed and vertical acceleration -g give flight time 2v sin(theta)/g when initial and final heights agree. Range is v² sin(2theta)/g. Complementary angles agree; 45 degrees maximizes this range.
The stream shows slowed steady trajectories as the nozzle angle changes, not the transient flow after a real nozzle adjustment. Air drag, breakup and unequal endpoint heights are excluded.

checks.description: Thirty and sixty degrees share a landing
Both return to the launch height

limitations: Numerical checks complement derivations. Idealized assumptions are stated; illustrative objects are not experimental data.
